classification.difficultyReason: Identify the discounted price as 80% of the original and scale back to 100%, following the taught reverse-percentage method.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The price of a dress has been discounted by $20\%$ and the discounted price is $\$96$. What was the original price?

answer.worked:
The discounted price represents $100\%-20\%=80\%$ of the original price.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Value of }80\%&=\$96\\\text{Value of }20\%&=\$96\div4=\$24\\\text{Value of }100\%&=\$24\times5=\$120\end{align*}$$

The original price was $\$120$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Water is flowing out of a dam at a constant rate of 200 litres per hour. How much water has flowed out of the dam in 3 hours?

answer.worked:
In 1 hour, 200 litres flows out.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Water flowing out in 3 hours}&=200\times3\text{ litres}\\\text{Water flowing out in 3 hours}&=600\text{ litres}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: If $10\%$ of a mine’s production in a day is 2100 tonnes, what is the total production for the day?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Production represented by }10\%&=2100\text{ tonnes}\\\text{Production represented by }100\%&=2100\times10\text{ tonnes}\\\text{Production represented by }100\%&=21\,000\text{ tonnes}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: If $70\%$ of an amount is $\$847$, what is the whole amount?

children.label: e
children.prompt: A car travels 96 km on 12 L of petrol. How much petrol would it use in travelling 200 km?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Petrol used for 1 km}&=\frac{12}{96}\text{ L}\\\text{Petrol used for 1 km}&=\frac18\text{ L}\\\text{Petrol used for 200 km}&=200\times\frac18\text{ L}\\\text{Petrol used for 200 km}&=25\text{ L}\end{align*}$$
